description: Verify that DUT silently discards a stray DHCPACK arriving in INIT (no preceding OFFER/REQUEST) — DUT must NOT treat itself as BOUND or emit any follow-up DHCPREQUEST (RFC 2131 §4.4.1 MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
A DHCPACK only has meaning at the end of a DISCOVER → OFFER → REQUEST exchange. A lone ACK in INIT (no DISCOVER yet, or no REQUEST in flight) is either a leftover or an attacker's spoof. DUT must ignore it; treating it as a successful binding would let unsolicited servers hand the client an arbitrary IP.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. DUT starts in INIT (no DISCOVER yet, or DISCOVER with no matching OFFER).
2. Tester → DUT: lone DHCPACK

3. Observation:
   • DUT must NOT emit a DHCPREQUEST in response   ← key check

[Pass condition]
No DHCPREQUEST follows the lone ACK within the listen window.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_unexpected_request — DUT emitted REQUEST after a lone ACK (DUT mistakenly entered REQUESTING/BOUND)
• Fail_no_discover — DUT did not emit DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently discarded the lone INIT-phase ACK — normal
verdicts.Fail_unexpected_request: DUT emitted DHCPREQUEST after a lone ACK
verdicts.Fail_no_discover: No DUT DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window
